questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

The diagram shows an individual’s total utility from consuming glasses of fruit juice. total utility total utility O number of glasses of fruit juice How can this information help to derive the individual’s demand curve for fruit juice?

options.A: by revealing the individual’s marginal utility curve
options.B: by revealing the money value of marginal utility
options.C: by showing how total utility is maximised
options.D: by showing the relationship between utility and expenditure

20 quantity of X The consumer’s income increases from $80 to $120 and, at the same time, the prices of X and Y change. If the consumer’s budget line is now RS, what are the new prices of X and Y? price of X ($) price of Y ($)
What will result from the differences in the non-pecuniary advantages of various occupations?

options.B: long-term differentials in wage rates
options.D: shortages of labour in particular occupations

questions.questionText: Which diagram correctly shows the relationship between the average product (AP) and the marginal product (MP) of labour, given that the quantities of other factor inputs remain constant? B A MP MP AP AP average average product, product, marginal marginal product product O O labour labour D C average average product, product, marginal marginal product product AP MP MP AP O O labour labour

A firm currently pays its employees on an hourly basis. Even though the management acknowledges that its employees work to the best of their ability and could not work any harder, the firm decides to switch to a piece-rate system of remuneration whereby the wage paid to each employee depends on their level of output. Why might this new system of remuneration result in a significant improvement in labour productivity?

options.A: It will dispense with the need for management to monitor the actions of its employees.
options.B: It will increase the losses that workers will incur if they are dismissed for not working hard enough.
options.C: It will lead to the recruitment and retention of more highly talented workers.
options.D: It will strengthen the incentives for workers to increase their earnings.

questions.questionText: A fashion model is paid $500000 a year. If the next best paid job he could get is as a teacher at $100000 a year, what are his transfer earnings and his economic rent? transfer earnings economic rent $ $
A fourfold increase in all of a firm’s inputs results in a threefold increase in its output. What does this illustrate?

options.B: economies of scale

questions.questionText: A firm employs two factors of production. The table shows the marginal products of these factors and their respective costs at the current level of output. land labour marginal
A firm, operating in an imperfectly competitive market, produces at the level of output where the price elasticity of demand for its product is equal to unity. What has the firm achieved?

options.B: maximum profits

questions.questionText: The table shows the five-firm concentration ratios for a selection of industries in an economy. percentage of total sales industry accounted for by the five largest firms in the industry (%) tobacco 95 steel 60 water supply 60 printing 12 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: The firms are of equal size in the steel industry and the water supply industry.
options.B: The printing industry is more competitive than the tobacco industry.
options.C: The tobacco industry is a monopoly market.
options.D: There are more firms in the tobacco industry than in the water supply industry.

options.A: OJ B OK C OL D OM

questions.questionText: Instead of charging all of its customers the same price, a firm decides to charge different prices in different markets. How is this likely to affect consumer surplus and the firm's marketing costs? consumer surplus marketing costs

options.B: decrease increase

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve, D , and supply curve, S , of a perfectly competitive

options.B: decreases increases

questions.questionText: A country has a negative income tax. In the diagram, the curve NT shows the country’s initial tax schedule. + NT tax NT income – What could cause the tax schedule to shift to NT ?

options.B: a more equal distribution of income
options.C: an increase in household disposable income
options.D: an increase in the marginal propensity to consume

options.A: $100 million B $120 million C $140 million D $240 million

questions.questionText: Which represents an injection into a country’s circular flow of income?

options.B: interest payments on government bonds
options.C: the payment of dividends to foreign shareholders

questions.questionText: Over one year the money income in an economy increased by 6%. In the same period prices rose by 4%. What can be concluded from this?

options.B: The velocity of circulation decreased by 2%.
options.D: The volume of output increased by 2%.

questions.questionText: What is likely to be the effect on interest rates and the supply of money of a purchase of government securities by a central bank? interest rates money supply

options.B: increase decrease

questions.questionText: The table shows the figures for consumption, capital formation and depreciation in four economies, all measured in US $. Assuming that the state of technology remains unchanged, which economy is most likely to experience economic growth? capital consumption capital formation economy depreciation ($ million) ($ million) ($ million)

Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per head is an indicator sometimes used to compare living standards of various countries. GDP is converted into a common currency at market exchange rates. What might cause this indicator to exaggerate the relative position of an individual country?

options.A: a high level of female participation in the labour force
options.B: a high level of foreign ownership in domestic industry
options.C: a high level of subsistence farming
options.D: relatively low hours worked by the labour force

questions.questionText: In the absence of offsetting changes, what will result in an increase in a government’s fiscal deficit?

options.B: a decrease in interest rates on government bonds
options.C: a decrease in private sector investment
options.D: a decrease in the country’s trade deficit

questions.questionText: An economy is operating at its natural rate of unemployment. According to monetarist theory, what will be the effect on unemployment in the short run and in the long run of an unanticipated increase in the money supply? short run long run

options.B: no change reduction

questions.questionText: What are likely to be the impacts on an economy of increased competition from abroad? impact on impact on trade impact on rate unemployment balance of inflation rate

options.B: improve reduce decrease

questions.questionText: An economy has underemployed resources. Which method of financing an increase in government expenditure is likely to have the greatest expansionary effect?

options.B: borrowing from the non-bank private sector

questions.questionText: The table shows how the government finances its budget deficit in a closed economy. $ budget deficit 200 billion sale of government securities to the central bank 50 billion sale of government securities to the non-bank private sector 150 billion If there is no change in notes and coins in circulation and commercial banks maintain a 10% cash reserve ratio, what will be the resulting increase in the money supply?

options.B: $150 billion

questions.questionText: What is likely to be the effect on developing economies of an increase in inward foreign direct investment?

options.B: an increase in the burden of debt
options.C: an increase in visible trade deficits

questions.questionText: Economists have proposed that the best policy to promote development is ‘trade not aid’. What is implied by this proposal?

options.B: Developing countries should be given greater access to markets in developed countries.
options.C: Developing countries should use foreign aid to invest in their export industries.
